note: The parser turns the input pattern token into a subexpression call, so the user-controlled regex text becomes a call node.
The look-behind validator recursively inspects the called node tree to decide whether the call is allowed inside look-behind.
A call node inside look-behind is delegated to the called body, propagating the input-controlled structure into the validator.
The safety obligation is that the look-behind body must not contain disallowed constructs; if validation misses a problematic recursive/call structure, compilation proceeds unsafely.
This is the rejection point for invalid look-behind patterns; the bug manifests when an invalid pattern is not rejected and later reaches the engine.
